companies.title: Companies
companies.description: One per line. A company domain (figma.com), a careers page or job board URL (https://jobs.lever.co/palantir), a board token with its ATS (greenhouse:stripe), or just a company name (notion). Domains are checked for a linked job board first; names are tried against each ATS.

keywords.title: Job title keywords
keywords.description: Keep jobs whose title contains any of these, e.g. "engineer", "data". Case-insensitive.

locations.title: Locations
locations.description: Keep jobs whose location contains any of these, e.g. "London", "United States". "Remote" also matches jobs flagged remote.

remoteOnly.title: Remote only
remoteOnly.description: Keep only jobs the board marks as remote, or whose location says remote.

departments.title: Departments
departments.description: Keep jobs whose department or team contains any of these, e.g. "Engineering".

postedWithinDays.title: Posted within (days)
postedWithinDays.description: Keep jobs first posted in the last N days. Jobs without a posting date are left out when this is set.

maxJobsPerCompany.title: Max jobs per company
maxJobsPerCompany.description: Newest first. Leave empty for no limit.

maxItems.title: Max jobs in total
maxItems.description: Stop after this many job rows across all companies. Company summary rows don't count.

includeDescriptionHtml.title: Include description HTML
includeDescriptionHtml.description: Add the original HTML description next to the plain-text one.

includeCompanyRows.title: Include company summary rows
includeCompanyRows.description: One free row per company with the detected ATS, open role count and department breakdown, or status "ats_not_found".

mode.title: Mode
enumTitles: Monitor: only jobs opened or closed since the last run
mode.description: Schedule monitor mode daily or weekly to track hiring changes.

monitorStoreName.title: Monitor memory name
monitorStoreName.description: Key-value store that remembers the previous job lists. Use a different name for each separate monitor.
